title: Rabbi Gamliel (V)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: His father, Rabbi Yehudah Nesia the second, was Rabbi Yochanan’s student; although he did not reach his fathers’ level, he was a great man. But his son Rabbi Gamliel did not reach his father’s level, by the testimony of Rabbi Abbahu in [Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.1.1.7): “Rabbi Abbahu said: And did not Rabban Gamliel Berabbi ask me whether it is permitted to go to a fair, and I forbade it to him? … How is that? Rabban Gamliel was a man of lesser standing, and Rabbi Abbahu wished to restrain him.” This Rabban Gamliel is likewise mentioned in [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.6.1.11): once he went down to stroll in his courtyard on Shabbat with a golden key in his hand, and his colleagues rebuked him.

Hyman writes that until Gamliel’s time the Patriarchs were based in Tzippori and Tiberias. He says the Christians then grew stronger in the Land of Israel and destroyed several Jewish towns, so Rabbi Abbahu, who enjoyed the government’s favor, took Gamliel under his protection in Caesarea. This is Hyman’s explanation for their appearing together. He suggests Gamliel may be the Patriarch whose household seized an orphan’s maidservant in the case he cites as Ketubot 24b (compare [Ketubot 84b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.84b.11)). Rabbi Abba objects that the household received favorable treatment.

He is likewise mentioned in Midrash Tehillim 100:9 (compare [Midrash Tehillim 20](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.20.5)): an incident in which Rabban Gamliel went to Rabbi Chelbo of Karuyah (the old Midrash Tehillim reads: to Abba Chalfa bar Kuriyah) and said to him, “Pray for me”; he said to him, “May He grant you according to your heart.” Abba Chalfa lived in the generation of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, which is the generation of this Rabban Gamliel. Hyman considers it very likely that the unnamed Patriarch in [Moed Katan 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.22b.21) — “The Patriarch died; Rav Chisda said to Rav Chanan bar Rabbah: Turn over the mortar and stand on it and show the rending to the world” — is this Rabban Gamliel. He explains in the entry Rav Chanan bar Rava that, because he was a native of the Land of Israel, Rav Chisda told him that he must show mourning over the Patriarch’s death. Since he was a man of lesser standing, his name is not mentioned. Hyman infers from this the time of his death, for it is known that Rabbi Yehudah Nesia the second died after Rav Yehudah, as explained in his entry; and this Rabban Gamliel died before Rav Chisda, who died in the year 620 of the Seleucid era (lishtarot). In his place sat Rabbi Yehudah Nesia the third, the father of Hillel, who established the calculation of intercalation.[^1]

notes.text: The consulted Ketubot 84b names the patriarchal household but leaves the Patriarch unnamed. Midrash Tehillim 20 names Chalfa ben Karuyah and records another version of the blessing. Moed Katan also leaves the deceased Patriarch unnamed and gives Rav Chanan bar Rava. The identifications, chronology and account of the move to Caesarea are Hyman’s reconstruction.
